mara: Quick Q — trying to add a deterministic automated test that reproduces SSE chunk-boundary partial-JSON + backpressure so our incremental parser and client buffer logic can be validated. Looking for a minimal, language-agnostic harness we can run in CI (no Docker heavy deps). Ideas?

jyoti: We wrote a tiny netcat/socat-based server a while back for this. Works well for byte-boundary fuzzing. Example: create a file with the exact bytes you want to stream and then use a loop to send small slices with sleeps. super simple.

jyoti: Example script (bash) — cuts a file into random-sized chunks and streams over HTTP/1.1 using ncat: 

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
PORT=9001
CONTENT_FILE=payload.ndjson   # each line is a JSON object or an SSE data: line
# start simple HTTP server to accept one connection
{ printf 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n'
  printf 'Content-Type: text/event-stream\r\n'
  printf 'Cache-Control: no-cache\r\n\r\n'
  # read bytes and stream in variable-sized chunks
  while IFS= read -r -n1 ch || [ -n "$ch" ]; do
    # send 1-6 bytes per tick to mimic fragmentation
    printf "%s" "$ch"
    # occasionally sleep to simulate backpressure
    if (( RANDOM % 50 == 0 )); then
      sleep 0.05
    fi
  done < "$CONTENT_FILE"
} | ncat -l $PORT -k
```

jyoti: You can generate the payload with mixed emojis/multibyte UTF-8 and long tokens to force split on rune boundaries.

ben: Another approach: use a tiny Node script that uses an http server and Writable stream with controlled `write` pacing. Easier to integrate into mocha/playwright tests. Also you can programmatically insert CRLFs and `data:` prefixes to exercise SSE parsing.

ben: Node example snippet: 

```
const http = require('http')
const payload = JSON.stringify({msg: 'hi 👋\u{1F3FD} big content...'})
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, {'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream'});
  const buf = Buffer.from('data: ' + payload + "\n\n")
  let i = 0
  const tick = setInterval(() => {
    const chunkSize = Math.max(1, Math.floor(Math.random()*8))
    res.write(buf.slice(i, i + chunkSize))
    i += chunkSize
    if (i >= buf.length) { clearInterval(tick); res.end(); }
  }, 10)
}).listen(9002)
```

alan: For the parser side we wrote a tiny table-driven test that feeds the client incremental byte arrays (not necessarily aligned to UTF-8 codepoints) and asserts the decoder emits the expected JSON once complete. If you only assert on final object equality you miss intermediate memory growth bugs.

mara: Nice, thanks. Two followups: 1) how do you assert consumer backpressure (i.e., client stops reading) without flakiness in CI? 2) any quick way to test multi-byte rune splitting (emoji) triggers no parser crashes?

jyoti: 1) Use an io.Pipe (or equivalent) so the server blocks on `Write` once buffer is full; on the client side measure that `Read` calls stop or the goroutine is backpressured. In node, check `socket.bufferSize` and assert it grows then eventually drains. In tests, use timeouts but keep them generous to avoid flakes.

jyoti: 2) For rune splits: generate payloads where you force a split inside a multibyte sequence. For example, 4-byte emoji. If you slice the buffer at 1..3 bytes you produce invalid UTF8 chunk boundaries. Make sure your incremental JSON parser uses a UTF-8 tolerant buffer (append raw bytes and decode only when a full codepoint is available) or rely on json.Decoder that reads from reader — but test it explicitly.

alan: Example small ruby/python helper to intentionally split a 4-byte rune across writes: 

```
# python
emoji = '\U0001F600'  # grinning face
payload = f'{"m": "a{emoji}b"}\n'
# send payload[:3], then payload[3:]
```

mara: Great. One more: how to validate we don't leak memory on client under sustained slow consumer?

sre-oncall: For Go use runtime/pprof to snapshot heap after X seconds of streaming and compare. For Node, run with `--inspect`/heap-profiler or use `memwatch` in CI to assert RSS stays within threshold. Also run with a long-lived streaming test and ensure GC is triggered periodically.

ben: We also added a cheap 'max-buffer-bytes' config in the SDK for clients which forces backpressure at the SDK level (erroring or dropping), and tests assert that path is exercised. Helps catch runaway buffering.

mara: Perfect. I'll prototype the netcat + random chunk script and add a deterministic payload generator for UTF-8 splits. Will upload a tiny test harness and link in the PR. Thanks all :heart: :thumbsup:
